plain_what: The project's first approach. Watch a conventional language model, record what it prefers in each context as a huge file of lookup tables, then answer by reading those tables with whole-number adds and comparisons only. It ran with no multiplication and matched the teacher on repetitive text, but never wrote coherent text on its own.
how_it_works: Offline, a teacher transformer (SmolLM2, GPT-2) is run over a corpus and its preferences are recorded. A compiler turns them into an R4G1 graph: a packed, content-addressed file holding records keyed by hashed context codes (recent-token n-grams and prefix regions), a cover of regions induced by entropy-gain splits, pre-quantised integer residual score tables per region, optional extra lanes (skip-mix candidate injection, segment, trajectory), and certificates comparing the graph to the teacher on held-out positions. At run time the engine hashes the recent tokens into a context code, takes the exact-context record or the best-matching region (nearest match over compact Hamming signatures, scored by a shift-add dot product in place of a multiply), accumulates the integer residuals in Q16.16 with saturation, counts each evidence contribution once, breaks ties deterministically and emits the best token. The frozen kernel contract permits only XOR, AND, OR, shifts, rotates, popcount, integer add and subtract, comparisons and table reads, with no float, multiply, divide or allocation after setup. Compilation, certification and every teacher forward pass are offline and unrestricted. Geometry (E8 and Hopf codes, zeta and prime routing, tropical routes) was tried as an indexing or scoring layer inside this frame.
geometry: Prime and zeta-phase routing keys, Hopf S3-to-S2 observation, E8-256 and 120-root codebooks for store vectors, H4/icosian frames, tropical (max-plus) route composition, VP-tree over Hamming signatures, Furey/Cayley-Dickson algebra modules (never wired into inference). Only the E8 codebook (beat sign codes at matched bits) and the integer shift-add dot kept measured value; the rest tied or lost.

status_reason: PARKED: compiled gains stayed teacher-forced and never became coherent free-running text (docs/free_running_reachability_840.md, docs/trajectory_routing_946.md INERT); the compiler path needs a banned transformer teacher and its float/softmax modules were retired by D36. Format and runtime kernel stay as a frozen, tested multiplier-free reference.
reopen_conditions: An owner decision on repair-or-retire of graph-compiler, graph-certify, api, proof-model and the root crate, which D36 item 3 flagged and left open.

A compile source that is not a banned transformer teacher: for example tables read out of the native discrete model, or the single donor corpus admitted by D41 (hard targets only, never for graph compilation unless a new decision says so).
A fresh D22 pre-registration with TEST FITNESS: FIT, at least two seeds, scored against lawful native references (D28) on free-running generation rather than teacher-forced agreement.
Adoption of the packed graph container and frozen kernel as the D11 export container for M4, with the export gap reported (D37).
Any added lane must show a served-token change at deployed reachability (the trajectory lane changed zero tokens).

rule_compat.D11: The frozen kernel is the ancestor of D11: only bitwise ops, shifts, popcount, integer add and subtract, comparisons and table reads, no float, multiply, divide or steady-state allocation (docs/inference_contract.md). Compliant as a kernel. Lookup is keyed by context code, but no per-token parameter-access count for the runtime was found in the records read, so D5-b status is unmeasured.
rule_compat.D23: Runtime scoring is softmax-free by contract (integer saturating residuals, docs/scoring_semantics.md). The offline path used teacher probabilities and log-probabilities (docs/probability_metadata_127.md); the retired transformerless compiler and runtime modules carry float and softmax content that D36 item 2 says is D23/D32-banned and may not be restored.
rule_compat.D30: Compiling needs a transformer teacher forward pass (Llama port, uor-matmul exact GEMM), which D25/D30 ban anywhere and D28 bans as a comparator or teacher. The frozen runtime itself contains no matmul (docs/matrix_operation_census.md).
rule_compat.D32_D37: D37 would allow float offline compilation, but the transformer teacher and probability machinery are separately banned. Nothing here is on the discrete GPU-only path, and the graph crates no longer build against the retired core.

experiments.configuration: Pinned honest harness over 16 interaction-residual candidate pairs (date is the issue opening date)
experiments.result: Every candidate degraded held-out scoring; a metric reading zero had hidden a real loss and the fake metric was reverted from main.
experiments.numbers: Rule 1 +0.64 to +2.25 bits/token (#102)

experiments.configuration: Phase B: shift-add dot product plus metric-consistent beam over a graded store (date is the issue opening date)
experiments.result: A much smaller integer store with zero multiplies matched and slightly beat the larger earlier store on the same measure.
experiments.numbers: 30.7 / 34.3 top-1 / agreement, 47,476 keys, multiplies 0, vs 28.2 / 31.9 for the previously shipped store (134,733 keys)

experiments.configuration: R4G1 graph path versus the same store read through the store path, 1,002-position subsample (date is the issue opening date)
experiments.result: A conversion/readout defect: same bytes, wrong decoder grammar; the graph scaffold was demoted and the store path unaffected.
experiments.numbers: graph path 0.0% top-1 / 0.0% agreement vs store path 28.2% / 31.9%, reproduced bit-for-bit 3 times

experiments.configuration: Corpus-scale sweep 150k to 500k records, shipped integer runtime against an f32 ceiling (date is the issue opening date)
experiments.result: No knee: gains continued log-linearly, and at 500k the integer runtime already beat the 150k f32 ceiling.
experiments.numbers: shipped 33.4 / 37.3 at 500k vs f32 ceiling 32.1 / 36.4 at 150k; about +1.5 to +1.8 points per doubling

failed_only_on_configuration: Graph readout 0.0% (#280): a decoder grammar defect on the same bytes that read 28.2% through the store path; says nothing about the graph format.
Skip-mix 41/87 (#897): caused by an eight-token candidate cap, fixed in #906 (projected 58/87).
Segment lane (#836): the reachable ceiling 19.0 permille sits just under a 20 permille floor on this bundle.
Trajectory lane INERT (#946): measured on one exact bundle where exact-context records dominate; the lane was compiled and reached but never changed a token.
Tropical routes (#626): the transition graph was self-loop dominated on that fixture.
Route-fit gate (#804): instrument vacuous because teacher attention is temporally smooth; the record calls it unreachable, not a verdict on route attention.
Phase-clock Design P rows (#392): rows built for that one design fell short; the phase idea survives elsewhere (zeta phases in the prime-zeta codebook).
open_questions: Is the packed R4G1 container a good export format for the discrete model, or should M4 use UORLUT01 only?
How much of the 29.5% ceiling is exact-context lookup (an n-gram table) rather than anything graph-specific?
Which of the 31 conformance ids registered for RF-31 are still true after #933 reclassified the lane as off-serving?
Do the Furey and Cayley-Dickson modules, never wired into inference, deserve a first real wiring test?

figure_ideas: A teacher-as-notebook picture: a large model's preferences on thousands of contexts being copied into rows of a table, then at run time one context hashed to a row and scored by additions, with the multiply symbol crossed out.
A ceiling bar chart on the broad-text panel: unigram floor 26.82%, any-k oracle 27.51%, shipped 29.52%, teacher agreement, so a reader sees how little room the store had under a lookup-only design.
